title: Integral prolongation of a given split rational reductive group
statement:
Let $(G_{\mathbf Q},T_{\mathbf Q}=D_{\mathbf Q}(M))$ be a split realization over $\mathbf Q$ of a finite reduced root datum $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ in the sense of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with the base and pinning forgotten. There exists a split realization $(\mathcal G,\mathcal T=D_{\mathbf Z}(M))$ of the same datum over $\mathbf Z$, and a $\mathbf Q$-group-scheme isomorphism
$$\iota:(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q},\mathcal T_{\mathbf Q})\xrightarrow{\sim}(G_{\mathbf Q},T_{\mathbf Q})$$
whose restriction to $D_{\mathbf Q}(M)$ is the identity and which respects the specified root and coroot labels. The term split realization includes smoothness, affineness, finite presentation, connected reductive geometric fibres, the full torus tangent decomposition with zero summand $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal T)$, and free rank-one integral root modules, exactly as in the cited definition. No base, pinning or generators are prescribed in the input or output. Roots need not span $M$; empty roots and rank zero are allowed. Thus the assertion extends an already given rational group and its specified torus, rather than postulating a group from an abstract datum.

source.place: Section 6.3, printed pp.212--229: Lemma 6.3.1 reduces by central products and diagonalizable central quotients to the semisimple simply connected case; the construction starts with a given split Q-group; Propositions 6.3.15 and 6.3.16, pp.227--229, give reductive geometric fibres and affineness, and the final paragraph gives the original generic fibre and free integral root lines. Generic-fibre identification in the central reductions uses the full-faithfulness part of Corollary 6.1.15, proved before integral existence. Read online; local PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this prolongation theorem.

proof.text: First carry out the construction for an arbitrary rational split realization of a datum with $\Phi$ spanning $M_{\mathbf Q}$ and $\mathbf Z\Phi^\vee=M^\vee$. Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-birational-integral-envelope] to obtain $H$, its torus and root homomorphisms, the fibrewise dense open product chart, and $H_{\mathbf Q}\simeq G_{\mathbf Q}$ fixing the specified torus. No integral reductivity has been used.

The chart in step 1 is geometrically irreducible and fibrewise dense, so each geometric fibre of $H$ is connected. Apply [lem-sfb-root-cell-semisimplicity-criterion] to every fibre: the same root datum, monomial torus action, rank-one identity and Weyl word all base change from the envelope. The fibres are affine semisimple with the specified torus, roots and coroots. Now [lem-sfb-relative-semisimple-affineness], with $B=\mathbf Z$, proves that $H$ is affine over $\mathbf Z$. Its immersed torus is a monomorphism; [lem-sfb-affine-multiplicative-type-monomorphism-closed] makes it a closed subgroup.

Differentiate the open product chart at $(0,1,0)$. Its differential is an isomorphism from $\operatorname{Lie}(D_{\mathbf Z}(M))\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathbf Z$ onto $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. Conjugation on the chart acts trivially on the torus tangent and as multiplication by the full character $\chi_\alpha$ on the $\alpha$ coordinate, by the envelope identities. Thus its zero summand is exactly the torus tangent and each root summand is a free line; this calculation is an identity on dual-number points over every algebra, without differentiating a character. Along with step 2 these are precisely all conditions of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] after forgetting the base and generators. We have proved the required prolongation for every semisimple simply connected datum, including the zero datum.

source.place: Tangent calculation preceding Proposition 6.3.15 and final paragraph of Section 6.3, pp.227--229

proof.text: For the given rational group, [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ realizes the lattice reflections inside a finite Weyl group. Thus their subgroup in $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ is finite. Return to the original arbitrary datum $\mathcal R$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding], with $V=\mathbf Q\Phi$ and $Z$ the annihilator of the coroots. It gives the weight lattice $P\subset V$, the free central lattice $C=\pi_Z(M)$, and a finite-index injection $j:M\hookrightarrow P\oplus C$ satisfying $j(\alpha)=(\alpha,0)$ and $\alpha^\vee(m)=\bar\alpha^\vee(\pi_Vm)$. The datum on $P$ with roots $\Phi$ and these restricted coroots is semisimple and simply connected: its dual is the coroot lattice by the defining integral-dual formula for $P$. It satisfies the hypotheses of step 1. Obtain its rational realization from [lem-sfb-rational-split-root-realization], and apply steps 1--3 to it, obtaining a split integral realization $S$ with torus $D_{\mathbf Z}(P)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.1, pp.212--213, central-torus and weight-lattice reductions

proof.text: Put $K=S\times D_{\mathbf Z}(C)$, with torus $T_K=D_{\mathbf Z}(P\oplus C)$. The product is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] and smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], applied to its tensor-product coordinate algebra, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to pass between the ring and scheme formulations. Finite presentations tensor to a finite presentation. The torus is reductive: a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup maps trivially to each multiplicative coordinate by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. The split-torus fibre is geometrically connected (its Laurent polynomial ring stays a domain after every field extension); [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] then makes its product with the connected fibre of $S$ connected. Every geometric fibre of $K$ is therefore smooth and connected, and is reductive by [lem-sfb-subdirect-product-reductivity] applied to the entire product, whose two projections are surjective. The product clause of [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-borel-root-compatibility], applied to the identity isogeny of each product fibre, identifies its roots and coroots with those of $S$; the tangent module is the direct sum of those of $S$ and the rootless torus, so $K$ is a split realization on $P\oplus C$, with roots $(\alpha,0)$ and coroots $(\bar\alpha^\vee,0)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.1, product with the split central torus, pp.212--213

proof.text: Let $N=D_{\mathbf Z}((P\oplus C)/j(M))\subset T_K$. Diagonalizable character duality identifies this as the kernel of $D(j):T_K\to D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$, and identifies $T_K/N$ with $D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$. Every root $(\alpha,0)=j(\alpha)$ vanishes on $N$; the centre formula [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] therefore puts $N$ in $Z(K)$ scheme-theoretically. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-quotient] over the nonzero Noetherian ring $\mathbf Z$ to form $\mathcal G=K/N$. It is reductive, with closed maximal torus $\mathcal T=T_K/N=D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$; formation of the quotient and torus commutes with arbitrary base change. In particular there is no assumption that $N$ is smooth or that its order is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.1, finite central diagonalizable quotient, pp.212--213

proof.text: For every geometric field, the quotient $K\to\mathcal G$ has finite central kernel. Apply [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-borel-root-compatibility] with $H=K_k$ and $G=\mathcal G_k$, both already known reductive. It identifies roots under pullback $j$ and coroots under $j^\vee$. The identities in step 4 give exactly $\Phi$ and $\Phi^\vee$ on $M$, with all labels fixed. For the integral tangent clause, [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] gives the direct weight decomposition, finite projective weight modules, and their base change. [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] identifies its zero summand with $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal T)$ and identifies the nonzero weight ranks with geometric root multiplicities. Thus the only nonzero summands off zero are the prescribed root lines. They have rank one everywhere and are free over $\mathbf Z$: a finite projective module is a summand of a finite free module, hence free by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free]. Consequently $\mathcal G$ is a split realization of the original datum with precisely the full tangent decomposition of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization].

source.place: Lemma 6.3.1 and root/tangent compatibility in Section 5.1; final paragraph of Section 6.3, pp.212--213,229

proof.text: First, $(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q},\mathcal T_{\mathbf Q})$ is a split realization over $\mathbf Q$ of $\mathcal R$: the base $\Delta$ of $\Phi$ supplied in step 4 (a condition on the finite set $\Phi\subset\mathbf Q\Phi$ only) is a base of $\mathcal R$, a generator of each free root line $\mathfrak g_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Delta$, makes $\mathcal G$ pinned, and [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change] along $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$ gives a pinned, hence split, realization with root lines $\mathbf Q\otimes\mathfrak g_\alpha$; then forget base and pinning. Apply [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting] over $\mathbf Q$ to the two split realizations $(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q},\mathcal T_{\mathbf Q})$ and the given $(G_{\mathbf Q},T_{\mathbf Q})$, taking $h=\mathrm{id}_M$ and the identity root bijection. The lemma gives a group isomorphism $\iota$ whose torus restriction is $D_{\mathbf Q}(\mathrm{id}_M)$, hence the identity, with the specified root and coroot labels. This is the asserted prolongation of the given rational pair. No pinning was prescribed; all temporary choices may be forgotten. For empty roots step 4 has $P=0$ and $C=M$, and $N=1$, so the construction is the split torus itself; for $M=0$ it is the trivial group.

source.place: Corollary 6.1.15 and central Isogeny Theorem preceding existence, pp.195--196; Lemma 6.3.1, pp.212--213
